title: Client Signal Compendium — Short Reads (March 2026)
content:
Purpose and usage notes:
- Short, scannable compendium of recent customer threads (last 8 weeks) with suggested low-effort fixes and 1–2 hypotheses for product/eng follow-up. Meant for quick handoff to PM/Eng on Monday syncs.
- This is intentionally terse — link to deeper notebooks where appropriate.

Topline themes (short reads):
1) Latency tail pain for bursty chat flows
   - Customers: two mid-market SaaS (fintech bot), one enterprise search partner.
   - Symptom: occasional 600–1,200ms token generation spikes during concurrent user bursts. Users report perceived slowdown and throttled UX.
   - Typical workaround in field: smaller request batch size, lowering max_tokens, degrade to lower-capacity model.
   - Quick hypothesis: KV cache misses + cold warmup of GPU kernels for >1 concurrent streams.
   - Suggested quick win: add an infra knob to keep one warm worker per region pinned during peak windows (configurable per-customer). Low dev:config + ops play.
   - Rough impact estimate: reduces reported tail spikes for 60% of observed incidents; ~1–2% extra infra cost.

2) Confusing routing behavior when dedicated pools are constrained
   - Customers: 3 Dedicated customers requested clearer fallback logs and SLA-visible routing decisions.
   - Symptom: unexpected failovers to hosted variants without customer-visible reason; support load increases.
   - Ask: expose 'route_reason' in API response header and console timeline for last 10 requests.
   - Implementation note: small API header change + console trace row.
   - Low lift, high signal: helps CS and customer debug; reduces ticket back-and-forth.

3) Embeddings stability and occasional quality drift after quantized model rollouts
   - Customers: 2 search/indexing customers on dedicated; noticing neighbor-distance shifts post-quantization.
   - Symptom: re-rank downstream accuracy dips, manual re-tuning required.
   - Proposed path: add a light-weight embedding-regression check (nightly) and auto-flag drift > threshold.
   - Trade: requires storing small eval set (customer-provided or synthetic) and a daily compute job.

Micro-vignettes (raw snippets):
- "We use Redwood for answers in product pages — some mornings we see the suggestions get worse and our re-ranker picks the wrong assets." — Customer A (notes: likely quantization/float->int rounding).
- "When we hit traffic spikes at 10am PST the bot gets choppy. Rebooting pool helps temporarily." — Customer B (ops workaround).

Prioritized quick-fix list (ranked by CS triage):
- P1 (fast): expose route_reason header + console event (owner: product-console; est dev: 2d).
- P1 (fast): add region warm-worker toggle for Peak windows (owner: infra-serving; est dev: 3d + ops-runbook).
- P2: nightly embedding-regression job + alert (owner: applied-ml; est dev: 1w + infra).
- P2: KV-cache diagnostic flags surfaced in logs (owner: serving-runtime; est dev: 4d).
- P3: customer-visible rollback button for recent model rollouts in dedicated console (owner: product-dedicated; est dev: 2w).

Engineering cost/benefit quick math (very rough):
- route_reason header + console UI: ~10 engineering days total, potential to cut 25% of routing-clarity tickets (saves ~1.5 FTE support time/week across top 10 customers).
- Warm-worker pin: infra + ops ~5 eng-days, recurring infra cost +1–2% per region during windows. Potential to eliminate 40% of burst-induced tail incidents.

Unresolved questions / things to validate with customers:
- For warm-worker idea: acceptable cost delta? Which customers want opt-in vs default?
- For embedding regression: do customers prefer providing a seed eval set or do we host a generic set and let customers opt-in to testing?
- How much telemetry can we safely collect for KV-cache misses without expanding PII risk? (Security review needed)

Links to specific tickets and threads (contextual):
- CS-8342: latency pattern diag from Customer B (includes logs).
- GH PR-119: console event timeline prototype (UI bits).
- Confluence: field-notes-runbook — longer raw threads and call transcripts.

Small UX/Docs patches that are low-effort and high-help:
- Add a short FAQ line on dedicates: "What happens if my pool is full" and link to a trace example. (owner: docs; est: 1d)
- Add example header to API quickstart showing route_reason and a sample value. (owner: devx; est: 1d)

Quick follow-up plan for next 2 weeks (sprint-ready actions):
- Mon (3/15): PM sync — present P1 quick-fixes (route_reason + warm-worker opt).
- Tue (3/16): engineering spike — infra team to prototype warm-worker toggle (2d).
- Wed (3/17): design + devx to add API header example (1d).
- Fri (3/19): CS to run lightweight customer poll (top 12 dedicated customers) re: warm-worker opt-in/cost tolerance.

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider a lightweight 'traffic-simulator' tool in sandbox to reproduce burst tail locally for customers. Not urgent but would help repro.
- Could we include a "why this happened" microsnippet in the console timeline (auto-generated by rules)? Signal: KV-cache cold miss -> show message.

Appendix: raw signals (short extracts)
- 2026-02-10 09:14 PST — Customer B incident: tokens per request unchanged, concurrency +3x -> 900ms tail. Log: step 'kv_lookup' had 0.8s gap. (see CS-8342)
- 2026-02-21 14:02 — Customer C: "embeddings seem noisier after the recent dedicated roll" (support thread attached).

If you want a deeper splice (full threads + transcripts) point to Confluence field-notes-runbook. Otherwise this doc is for quick pick-and-run actions.

-- Maya
